description.en: OntoGSN is an ontology for managing assurance cases in the Goal Structuring Notation (GSN). The goal of the ontology is to help users in linking the elements of their cases - claims and evidence - with the internationalized resource identifiers (IRIs) of represented concepts, events and data, and in evaluating the validity of their argument.

note.value: A definition prefixed [OntoGSN] is this ontology’s wording, not the GSN Community Standard’s. Every definition, tagged or not, has a record in the provenance graph naming the passage it rests on, or stating that it rests on none.

source.value: The Assurance Case Working Group (ACWG). (2021 May). Goal Structuring Notation Community Standard Version 3. URL: http://scsc.uk/SCSC-141C

contributor.value: Barbara Gallina, Dian Balta, Ingmar Kessler

definition.value: GSN is a graphical argument notation which can be used to document explicitly the elements and structure of an argument and the argument’s relationship to evidence.

note.value: Membership of this class is only meant to be inferred, not asserted! Please do not add individuals to this class manually (i.e., assertions).

The goal and solution statements should be clearly expressed such that the crux of the challenge is unequivocally communicated. Thus, the link between the part of the argument that is being challenged (target) and the dialectic element (source) is self-evident.

definition.value: The source of challenge being applied; can be directed at any part of an argument. A defeater (goal or solution) can challenge any element in a goal structure, e.g. goal, solution, strategy, context, assumption, justification.
A solution, rendered as a circle, presents a reference to an evidence item.
A body of information presented with the intention to establish one or more claims through the presentation of related supporting claims, evidence and contextual information.
A connected series of claims intended to establish an overall claim.
A context, rendered as shown left, presents a contextual artefact. This can be a reference to contextual information, or a statement.

This symbol indicates that the GSN argument below the attached element is to be instantiated as a template argument. It provides a reference to the information used to instantiate the template argument.

A pattern catalogue may be created to collate a series of patterns; where such a catalogue is created the structure and format of the definition should be consistent and each pattern’s definition should have a unique {pattern identifier}.
The argument view depicts the argument inside an individual module.
Arguments and evidence intended to demonstrate that a system meets its assurance requirements.
A reasoned and compelling argument, supported by a body of evidence, that a system, service or organisation will operate as intended for a defined application in a defined environment.
A justification, rendered as an oval with the letter 'J' at the top- or bottom-right, presents a statement of rationale.
A template argument is a special case of a pattern argument. It uses the core GSN and argument pattern extension to construct an argument structure which requires no further development.
An assumption, rendered as an oval with the letter 'A' at the top- or bottom-right, presents an intentionally unsubstantiated statement.

note.value: The corresponding argument could be located in a paragraph of accompanying text, a goal in the local argument, or a goal in a separate module.

definition.value: [OntoGSN] A relationship carrying an assurance claim point, whose associated confidence argument documents the reasons for having confidence in the relationship between two elements.
Goals, solutions, strategies, contexts, assumptions and justifications form the principal elements of GSN.
[OntoGSN] An element that makes no claim of its own and instead points at an artefact, such as a solution or a context expressed as a noun phrase.
[OntoGSN] A link between GSN elements treated as an individual in its own right, carrying its subject, object and type, so that the link itself can be decorated and described.
[OntoGSN] A reusable argument structure, accompanied by a description that defines its intent and the constraints on its use, from which concrete arguments are instantiated.
A strategy, rendered as a parallelogram, describes the inference that exists between a goal and its supporting goal(s).
A goal, rendered as a rectangle, presents a claim forming part of the argument.
(Claim is) A proposition being asserted by the author that is a true or false statement.
[OntoGSN] Information or objective artefacts (e.g., files) being offered in support or context of one or more claims.

renderedAs.value: a rectangle with a second smaller rectangle adjoining at the top left

definition.value: Goal structures can be partitioned into separate, but interrelated, modules. This can allow the division of an overall goal structure into separate goal structures focusing on particular aspects of the overall argument. A module may contain one or more arguments and may contain other modules.
The attached element remains to be instantiated: at some later stage the abstract element needs to be replaced with a more concrete instance.

note.value: Contract modules can be used in the support relationship between modules to aid decoupling. The de-coupling by use of a contract permits argument module construction in cases where the eventual source of support for an argument is unknown at the time of authoring or can be changed for example through re-use or planned product improvement or reconfiguration.
A contract may be described in textual form (e.g. as a table) or for more complex relationships may be described within a contract module using GSN.

renderedAs.value: a rectangle with two smaller rectangles (of equal size to each other) adjoining at the top left and bottom right

definition.value: A contract module is a special type of module that controls the relationship between argument module interfaces using arguments to define how a goal in one module is supported by one or more goals in one or more other modules.

The dialectic challenge within this structure asserts that if the claim presented in Goal CG1 is true then this is sufficient to establish that the claim in Goal G1 in the original structure is in doubt.

description.en: An away assumption repeats an assumption presented in another argument module and is typically used only in Contract Modules. An away context repeats a reference to context presented in another argument module. An away goal reference repeats a claim presented in another argument module. An away justification repeats a justification presented in another argument module and is typically used only in Contract Modules. An away solution repeats a reference to evidence items presented in another argument module.

renderedAs.value: bisecting line in the lower half

definition.value: An away element reference repeats a claim or evidence presented in another argument module.
[OntoGSN] The text the element asserts, written to the grammatical rules the standard sets for GSN statements.
SupportedBy, rendered as a line with a solid arrowhead, allows support relationships between elements to be documented.

By making the relationship to the away goal the author is asserting not only the inference of support for the parent goal, but also that the context in which the away goal is declared is consistent with the context and assumptions in scope for the parent goal.
[OntoGSN] The text the element asserts, written to the grammatical rules the standard sets for GSN statements.
[OntoGSN] Determines whether the argument at this element continues in, or is a continuation from, a separate diagram.

note.value: Inferred, never authored. A module contains arguments and other modules, so the module an element belongs to is always reached in two steps or more. This property names the result of that traversal so that the rules of the Modular Extension can state it in one atom. It is derived by the Module Membership and Nested Module Membership rules.

definition.value: The module an element belongs to, whether the element sits in an argument the module contains or in a module nested inside it.
[OntoGSN] Links a relationship or an artefact reference to the confidence argument provided for it.

[OntoGSN] Defines the kind of argument this is: a risk argument (i.e., the main content of assurance), a confidence argument for an assurance claim point, a compliance argument (undefined in the normative standard), or a dialectic argument.
Undeveloped element decorator, rendered as a hollow diamond applied to the bottom centre of an element, indicates that a line of argument has not been developed.
A GSN choice can be used to denote possible alternatives in satisfying a relationship.
SupportedBy, rendered as a line with a solid arrowhead, allows support relationships between elements to be documented.
[OntoGSN] The text the element asserts, written to the grammatical rules the standard sets for GSN statements.

Optional instantiation means that the relationship and the argument below may or may not be instantiated.
This section can be used to reference patterns that are related e.g. addressing the same intent in a different context.
InContextOf, rendered as a line with a hollow arrowhead, declares a contextual relationship.
[OntoGSN] Determines whether the view shows the argument or the module architecture.

description.en: Defeated Relationship indicates that the relationship is defeated. The Defeated decorator can be applied to any of the GSN relationships.

definition.value: This decorator symbol indicates that the element is defeated. The Defeated decorator can be applied to any of the GSN elements.

definition.value: Support for the claim presented by the attached goal is intended to be provided from an argument in another module linked by an as-yet-undisclosed contract.
[OntoGSN] Relates an artefact reference or an instantiation data reference to the artefact it points at.
[OntoGSN] The upper bound on how many instances of the related element this relationship stands for.

A GSN Goal that presents the pinnacle claim in an argument. It is ‘top’ in terms of the argument hierarchy, rather than necessarily its physical layout. There may be more than one top goal in a GSN structure.
The top goal presents the overall claim asserted by the author and it is up to the reader to determine their belief that it is adequately supported.
[OntoGSN] Marks whether the element is determined (e.g., by a GSN rule) to be consistent or otherwise correct with respect to the GSN argument syntax.
[OntoGSN] Marks whether the claim in the element or relationship is determined (e.g., by the auditor or some process) as correct or not.
A particular kind of argument where the relationships between the asserted claims, and from the evidence to the claims, are explicitly represented.

There may be occasions when a goal or strategy requires fuller justification than can be provided within the confines of a GSN justification element. In such cases, an away goal can be substituted for the justification.

An evidential relationship is a declared relationship between a claim and an evidence item by which the claim is substantiated. An inferential relationship is a declared inference between claims in the argument. A contextual relationship draws attention to explanatory contextual information.

SupportedBy relationships – represented by lines with solid arrowheads – indicate inferential or evidential relationships between elements. InContextOf relationships – represented as lines with hollow arrowheads – declare contextual relationships.

definition.value: Allows a Challenge to any GSN entity to be documented. A goal, (core element) can be used in a dialectic context to assert a challenge to part of the argument. A solution, (core element) can be used to present a reference to an evidence item that asserts a challenge to part of the argument.

definition.value: This indicates that the element is publicly visible in one or more interfaces of the module and can be referenced as an away element.
[OntoGSN] Determines whether this is the delivered version of the argument or pattern, in which no element remains uninstantiated or undeveloped.
[OntoGSN] The text the element asserts, written to the grammatical rules the standard sets for GSN statements.
An Assurance Claim Point (ACP) can be used in GSN to indicate that a confidence argument is associated with an assertion in a risk argument.
[OntoGSN] Links an instantiation data reference to the element or template argument it annotates.
[OntoGSN] Determines whether the argument or pattern is in its published form, in which the undeveloped decorator is not permitted.
